title: DUAL SATELLITE IN-ORBIT TESTBED FOR SENSING AND COMMUNICATION FOR LOW-POWER DEVICES (ARTES AT 3E.034)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and launch a dual satellite in-orbit testbed for sensing and communication for low-power devices with both transmit and receive user capability and inter-satellite link.Targeted Improvements: Enabling the development of protocols and operations concepts for the communication and geolocation from space with low-power terrestrial devices.Description: There is currently no European in-orbit capability to test and validate low-power communication directlybetween LEO satellites and standard ground devices. This limits the development of protocols, modulation schemes, and system architectures for emerging applications in low-power geolocation, environmental sensing, and ubiquitous IoT connectivity. This activity will develop a test bed that supports the exploration of disruptive use cases in low power direct communications between terrestrialdevices and LEO satellites. The testbed will comprise two satellites operating in tandem that can (at a minimum):- Establish a bi-directional low power (Tx/Rx) communications link between satellite and terrestrial devices- Provide Inter-satellite links (ISL) between the two, supporting cross-traffic, redundancy as well as geolocation of devices and interference sources- Test new protocols (e.g. SigFox, LoraWan, Bluetooth) and modulation schemes optimised for low-power signals.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 with a budget of up to 3MEuro will design and develop a dual-satellite payload testbed able to directly communicate with terrestrial low-power devices. It will mature the key technologies and communication protocols from using simulation and laboratory testing to demonstrate feasibility and system readiness for in-orbit demonstration. Deliverables from Phase 1 are a summary report and full engineering model.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the dual-satellite platform toexperiment with direct low-power, low frequency communications in orbit. The in-orbit experiment will test real-time user communications, validate geolocation concepts, evaluate inter-satellite link performance and collect performance data to inform future protocol standardisation and system architectures. Deliverables from Phase 2 are a summary report and 2 x flight engineering models.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: S3-CL-14 - ZERO DEBRIS LARGE PLATFORMS PHASE 2
description: This activity supports the evolution of European large (> 1 ton) LEO satellite platforms in line with ESA's Zero Debris objective by 2030. Building on previous work performed with European system integrators, it will mature platform designs from System Requirements Review (SRR) to Preliminary Design Review (PDR) level while advancing key Zero Debris technologies towards operational readiness.The activity will address end-of-life disposal, resilience against failures, health monitoring, and preparation for removal throughthe development and integration of innovative platform technologies. It will combine system-level platform design activities with technology maturation and co-engineering between platform integrators and specialised technology suppliers. The overall objective isto enable the next generation of European satellite product lines, supporting the implementation of the Space Debris Mitigation policy while maintaining technical feasibility, competitiveness, and affordability.

title: ESA FIDUCIAL REFERENCE MEASUREMENT (FRM) ATLAS - EXPRO+
description: The ESA Fiducial Reference Measurement (FRM) Atlas is an Earth Observation initiative led by to develop an open-access platform forFRM and calibration/validationknowledge.FRMs are fully characterised, traceable measurements with documented uncertainties, used to assess the accuracy and quality of satellite products.ESA-supported FRM activities cover domains including ocean colour, altimetry, surface temperature, atmospheric composition, vegetation, soil moisture and radar.As their associated datasets, procedures and expertise are distributed across many platforms, a centralised mechanism is needed to improve accessibility and interoperability.TheAtlas will provide a single entry point for discovering FRM projects, datasets, procedures, campaigns, documentation, infrastructures and experts.It will connect FRMs with satellite missions, products, variables and validation methodologies,while federating existing resources rather than duplicating them.Its objectives are to improve discoverability, support best practices, promote knowledge reuse and harmonisation, and maximise the value of ESA's Cal/Val investments.

title: NAVISP-EL1-117-RESILIENCE TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR GNSS SPACE RECEIVERS IN INTERFERENCE, JAMMING AND SPOOFING CONDITIONS.
description: NAVISP-EL1-117-Resilience Techniques and Algorithms for GNSS Space Receivers in Interference, Jamming and Spoofing Conditions: Thisactivity aims to enhance the resilience of GNSS space receivers against interference, jamming, and spoofing in LEO. It will study and evaluate novel detection and mitigation techniques, including potential spin-in from terrestrial applications. The scope includesdefining standardized threats and scenarios to support future specifications for space receivers. The work involves simulations andearly prototyping of selected technologies to validate concepts. The goal is to maintain GNSS receiver performance during RFI events without monitoring or reporting interference. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity
